findings.problem: Server phone regex ^(?:\+91|91|0)?([6-9]\d{9})$ in Python matches Unicode digits (verified: '9८४८०१२३४५' matches, stored '+919८४८०१२३४५'). Stored phone is not ASCII +91XXXXXXXXXX; associates.contact_key keeps Unicode digits so the same number in another script gets a different key, bypassing insert-once/cool-down/no-revival and breaking deletion-by-contact; client (ASCII \d) and server diverge.
findings.fix: Use [6-9][0-9]{9} (or re.ASCII) in network.py; state 'ASCII digits only, other scripts invalid/phone'; add invalid vectors '9८४८०१२३४५' and full-width '９８４８０１２３４５' to phone.test.ts and api pytest.

findings.problem: JS /(?<!\d)(?:\d[\W_]*){11}\d(?!\d)/u is not equivalent to Python's Unicode-aware pattern (JS \d ASCII-only, JS \W matches Telugu letters).
findings.fix: Document the client mirror as ASCII-only and UX-only with the server authoritative; optionally use [^0-9A-Za-z] in place of [\W_] in JS.
